claims.text: Equiatomic NiTi shape-memory alloys display temperature-dependent plastic deformation behavior.
Temperature changes trigger a martensite-to-austenite phase transformation in NiTi.
The martensite-to-austenite transformation modulates dislocation mobility and deformation mechanisms.
The low-temperature state of equiatomic NiTi is martensitic.
The low-temperature martensitic phase has a twinned, low-symmetry structure.
Below the martensitic finish temperature, the alloy is predominantly martensitic.
Well above the transformation temperature, the alloy is predominantly austenitic.
The temperature-induced martensitic-to-austenitic transformation alters the crystal structure and changes dislocation mobility and twinning behavior.
At lower temperatures, martensite restricts dislocation mobility.
Restricted dislocation mobility in low-temperature martensite results in higher yield strength and lower ductility.
Transformation to austenite with increasing temperature enhances dislocation mobility and initiates pseudoelastic effects.
Enhanced dislocation mobility and pseudoelastic effects in the austenitic regime reduce yield strength and increase ductility.
Heating across the martensite-to-austenite transition will reproducibly decrease yield strength and increase ductility.
Composition or processing deviations that alter transformation temperatures or structural stability may change the deformation outcome.
The quantitative changes in yield strength and ductility may depend on specimen preparation and testing details.
